title: Show, explain, discuss and analyse the relationship between society and natural environment

lessons.title: How people depend on nature
lessons.html:
We are part of the environment

The natural environment is everything around us that was not made by people: soil, water, air, plants, animals, rivers, mountains and the weather. Society means all the people living together in families, villages, towns and the country.

People and nature are linked. We need nature to live, and what we do changes nature.

What nature gives us

  • Food: crops grow in soil with rain and sun; cattle, sheep and goats graze the veld.
  • Water: from rivers, dams, springs and boreholes for drinking, washing and irrigation.
  • Energy: firewood, sun, wind and coal.
  • Building materials: wood, thatch grass, clay, stone and sand.
  • Medicine: many traditional and modern medicines come from plants.
  • Clean air from plants and trees.
  • Income and jobs: farming, forestry, fishing and tourism in game reserves.

Culture and nature

In many South African communities, nature is part of culture and belief. Cattle show wealth and are used in lobola and ceremonies. Some rivers, mountains and trees are sacred places. Traditional knowledge tells people when to plant, how to read the weather and which plants heal.

Where people live

People usually settle where there is water and good soil. That is why towns grew next to rivers and why farming areas follow good rainfall. In dry areas such as the Karoo, farms are large and farmers keep sheep and goats that can live on little grazing. In areas with good rain, such as parts of KwaZulu-Natal and Mpumalanga, people grow sugarcane, maize, timber and vegetables.

lessons.title: How people change the environment
lessons.html:
Our impact on nature

Everything people do has an effect on the environment. Some effects are good, many are harmful.

Harmful effects

What people doWhat happens
Too many animals on the veld (overgrazing)Grass disappears, soil washes away, dongas form
Cutting trees for firewoodSoil erosion, less shade, animals lose their homes
Throwing rubbish and plasticPollution, animals eat plastic and die
Washing sprayers or dumping chemicals near riversWater is poisoned for people, fish and animals
Burning coal and dieselAir pollution and climate change
Ploughing steep slopesTopsoil washes into dams and rivers

Climate change

The climate is slowly changing. Many scientists say South Africa can expect more droughts in some areas, hotter summers and heavier storms. Farmers must adapt with drought-tolerant crops, water saving and good veld care.

Good effects

  • Planting trees and grass on bare land.
  • Building contours and gabions to stop erosion.
  • Rotational grazing so the veld can rest.
  • Making compost instead of burning waste.
  • Removing invasive alien plants such as wattle and prickly pear, which use lots of water.
  • Protected areas such as national parks.

Rules that protect the environment

South Africa has laws that protect the environment, such as the Conservation of Agricultural Resources Act 43 of 1983 and the National Water Act 36 of 1998. The Constitution also gives everyone the right to an environment that is not harmful to their health.

What you can do

Use water carefully, put rubbish in bins, never pour chemicals on the ground or in water, report fires and leaks, and look after the veld and soil.

Key points

  • People depend on nature for food, water, energy, medicine and jobs.
  • Nature is also part of culture and belief.
  • Overgrazing, pollution and cutting trees harm the environment.
  • Good practices such as rotational grazing and compost help the environment.
  • Laws and the Constitution protect the environment.

quiz.question: What can happen when there are too many animals on the veld?

options.text: Grass disappears and soil washes away

quiz.question: Why do farms in the Karoo usually keep sheep and goats?

options.text: Because the area is dry and these animals can live on little grazing
Because there is too much rain for crops
Because sheep do not need water

quiz.question: Why should invasive alien plants such as wattle be removed?

options.text: They give too much shade to cattle
They use a lot of water
